text: Hydrogen sulfide (H₂S) acts as a neuromodulator in the brain and is shown to be associated with cognitive impairments in schizophrenia. Atypical antipsychotics can provide cognitive benefits for schizophrenia patients. This prospective observational study aims to investigate whether H 2 S signaling is involved in the cognitive improvement effects of atypical antipsychotics in patients with schizophrenia.
source_label: Changes in plasma hydrogen sulfide are associated with cognitive improvements in schizophrenia patients treated with atypical antipsychotics
